title: Bridging Genomic Research Disparities in Osteoporosis GWAS: Insights for Diverse Populations.
authors: Wu, Qing; Dai, Jingyuan; Liu, Jianing; Wu, Lang
one_liner_zh: 该综述聚焦骨质疏松GWAS遗传位点与人群差异，虽提及RUNX2转录调控和机器学习，但核心是遗传关联与风险预测，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或TF-DNA结合机制研究，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have significantly advanced osteoporosis research by identifying genetic loci associated with bone mineral density (BMD) and fracture risk. However, disparities persist due to the underrepresentation of non-European populations, limiting the applicability of polygenic risk scores (PRS). This review examines recent advancements in osteoporosis genetics, highlights existing disparities, and explores strategies for more inclusive research. RECENT FINDINGS: European-focused GWAS have identified key loci for osteoporosis, including WNT signaling (SOST, LRP5) and RUNX2 transcriptional regulation. However, fewer than 40% of these variants can be replicated in Asian and African populations. Emerging studies in non-European groups reveal population-specific loci, sex-specific associations, and gene-environment interactions. Advances in machine learning (ML)-assisted GWAS and multi-omics integration are improving genetic discovery. Expanding GWAS in diverse populations, integrating multi-omics data, refining ML-based risk models, and standardizing biobank data are essential for equitable osteoporosis research. Future efforts must prioritize clinical translation to enhance personalized osteoporosis prevention and treatment.
abstract_zh: 综述目的：全基因组关联研究（GWAS）通过识别与骨密度（BMD）和骨折风险相关的遗传位点，显著推进了骨质疏松症研究。然而，由于非欧洲人群的代表性不足，多基因风险评分（PRS）的适用性受限，差异依然存在。本综述审视了骨质疏松症遗传学的最新进展，强调了现有差异，并探讨了更具包容性研究的策略。近期发现：以欧洲人群为重点的GWAS已识别出骨质疏松症的关键位点，包括WNT信号通路（SOST、LRP5）和RUNX2转录调控。然而，这些变异中不到40%能在亚洲和非洲人群中复制。非欧洲群体的新兴研究揭示了人群特异性位点、性别特异性关联及基因-环境交互作用。机器学习（ML）辅助GWAS和多组学整合的进展正在改善遗传发现。在多样化人群中扩展GWAS、整合多组学数据、优化基于ML的风险模型以及标准化生物库数据，对于公平的骨质疏松症研究至关重要。未来努力必须优先考虑临床转化，以增强个性化的骨质疏松症预防和治疗。
